content:
The new Apple TV 4K is long overdue, with the market originally expecting it to launch last fall. However, with Siri AI now finally ready, all signs point to a new Apple TV 4K being unveiled—possibly at the September 9 event. Here are the rumours currently circulating.

Point 1: Siri Remote update

Although no details have been revealed, Apple is reportedly set to release an updated Siri Remote for the new Apple TV 4K.

Code leaked from a test build of macOS 26.7 appears to confirm the existence of a new Siri Remote. And before this leak, Mark Gurman had already reported that the new hardware might come with a 'revamped Apple TV remote'.

It doesn't look like there will be major changes, but hopefully at least a second-generation ultra-wideband chip will be added to support Precision Finding.

Point 2: Siri AI and more Apple Intelligence features

Siri AI is expected to be the key selling point for the new Apple TV and other new home products.

As of now, Apple has not revealed whether the new assistant features will land on Apple TV 4K or HomePod. But mounting evidence suggests that tvOS 27 will include Siri AI—and likely only support the new hardware.

There's also a good chance we'll see other Apple Intelligence features, such as an enhanced search experience.

Point 3: New-generation A-series chip

The current Apple TV uses the A15 Bionic chip first released in 2021. The good news is that the new model is expected to see a significant performance boost.

The new device will feature a more powerful A-series chip to support AI capabilities.

Rumours suggest the new chip might be the A17 Pro or A18. However, most of these reports surfaced before the launch of Siri AI. It wouldn't be surprising if Apple instead equipped it with a more powerful A19 or A20 chip.

Point 4: N1 wireless chip

Hot take posted by Doug

Ideally, it should be able to replace older HomePod devices and support Siri AI features.

Second, it should have built-in microphones to receive Siri AI commands without using the remote.

Finally, it should deliver the long-promised universal TV remote functionality (which has been blocked by partners like Netflix) and let us query new shows across all streaming services, including cable providers.

Netflix's library data is public, so Siri AI can search through it as well as all other media content I have access to. Apple TV should become a universal set-top box.

Also, AirPlay should have long supported connecting to multiple HomePods for a true home theatre setup, including automatically calibrated Atmos audio.

The N1 wireless chip, reportedly debuting with the iPhone 17, is also expected to make its way into the new Apple TV 4K.

By adding the N1 chip, Apple will bring Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6 support to the Apple TV, along with Thread networking support.

By comparison, the current Apple TV hardware, now four years old, only supports Wi-Fi 6 and Bluetooth 5.

What features are you hoping to see in the new Apple TV 4K? Share them in the comments.
